card vi-onview  [decided]
One view = one card, detail on top, sub-cards below
why: No side panel. Every node has a page. The shape is identical at every depth.
subtree: 5 cards, 5 decided, 1 unchallenged

This is what makes it genuinely fractal. The same layout renders the root statement, the deepest leaf, and now a source node.

A leaf shows its full detail and an empty sub-card area, instead of an empty page — which is what version 2 did wrong.

The address bar carries the current node, so a view is shareable and survives a reload.

                                      decided requires, checked against the log, not the prose:

                                        - a kill criterion on record (see "werk kill")
                                      each missing fact fails with the command that fixes it

       [--text "..."]                 manual test, or the reason words for no-metric
       [--reason unclear|cheap|slow|values|constraint] [--review-date YYYY-MM-DD]

  werk kill-state <id> <n> monitored|unmonitored|fired [--detail "..."]
